approach: Find the total fall time, the distance covered in the last second from the nth-second formula, and express it as a percentage of the height.

steps.text: Use h = ½gt² to find the total time to fall the full height of the tower from rest.
Find the distance covered during the last, that is fifth, second using the nth-second formula for free fall from rest.
Express this distance as a percentage of the tower's height.

common_mistakes.text: Computing the last-second distance as the difference of squares of the times, 5² − 4² = 9, forgetting to multiply by ½g, and mistaking this raw number for the percentage.
Using (n+1)² = 36 in the denominator of the last-second fraction (2n−1)/n² instead of n² = 25, as if the fall lasted one second longer, gives 25% instead of the correct 36%.
No slip reaches 49%: subtracting the first four seconds' distance from the height gives 64%, and using the final speed alone as a fraction of the height gives 40%; nothing lands on 49%.
